929 AM EDT Tue Sep 15 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
No changes have been made to the forecast this morning.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Remaining cool today, with shower and thunderstorm chances
  returning late in the week and into the weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Remaining cool today, with shower and 
thunderstorm chances returning late in the week and into the 
weekend.

With a broad 1026-mb surface anticyclone anchored over the 
northeastern U.S., expect conditions to be fairly similar to 
yesterday/Monday. The one major difference will be the marked 
reduction in temperatures and humidity, as well as winds given 
weak gradients within the influence of this dome of high 
pressure. Today's high temperatures are forecast to reach the 
mid 70s to low 80s (upper 60s to low 70s in the mountains). This
comes with continued low humidity with dew points mainly in the
upper 40s to low 50s. Aside from some passing high cirrus, 
abundant sunshine is expected throughout the day. Light 
southeasterly gradients will favor an uptick in overnight 
temperatures. While still cooler than recent days, most can 
anticipate lows in the mid 50s to low 60s (mildest along the 
I-95 urban areas as well as near the Potomac River and 
Chesapeake Bay shorelines).

Behind an exiting longwave trough that pushes into the Canadian
Maritimes, mid/upper heights begin to build in earnest. An
expansive near 600-dm mid-level ridge initially over the 
southern U.S. will flex northward in time. These above average 
heights remain a fixture in the forecast through Thursday. This 
supports a return of warmer temperatures along with building 
humidity levels. Daily highs push back into the mid/upper 80s, 
locally reaching the low 90s in the warm spots. The return of 
the humidity also favors milder nights with widespread lows in 
the 60s. Any shower and thunderstorm chances should hold off 
until Thursday given the stout ridge aloft quelling most 
precipitation chances. Most models keep such a threat mainly 
west of the Shenandoah Valley, especially closer to the 
Alleghenies.

A high latitude trough digging across southeastern Canada should
be enough to nudge the upper ridge back toward the south-central
U.S. This allows a cold front to push through early Friday
which again brings a gradual cool down with decreasing humidity
into Saturday. However, this reprieve is somewhat brief as 
additional disturbances in the atmosphere track toward the area 
late in the weekend. The overall jet pattern turns a bit more 
complex as an array of features enter the picture. A broad 
upper low retrogrades across the Gulf. At the same time, a 
myriad of shortwaves will eject across the central U.S. toward 
the Mississippi Valley. How these impulses behave along with 
where surface features reside will dictate any local weather 
impacts. However, all signs point toward a more active pattern 
on Sunday into early next week.

&&

.AVIATION /13Z TUESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
Canadian high pressure will support VFR conditions through mid-
week. Weak gradients keep lighter winds than yesterday/Monday,
with winds gradually shifting from east to southeasterly today.
This ridge eventually edges toward the Atlantic coastline which
will support mainly southerly winds on Wednesday into Thursday.
Some storm chances emerge by Thursday, but these are currently
expected to stay west of the area TAF sites.

A cold front moves through early Friday which results in some
uptick in shower chances. This may come with a few restrictions
if convection becomes more pronounced. In the wake of this
frontal passage, winds turn more northerly with afternoon gusts
to around 15 knots or so. High pressure building to the north
results in an east to southeasterly wind for Saturday. This 
comes with likely VFR conditions.

&&

.MARINE...
Gradients will continue to weaken through the day with winds 
around 5 to 10 knots.

High pressure slowly pushes away toward the coast which results
in a south to southeasterly wind for Wednesday and Thursday. 
Some southerly channeling effects may necessitate Small Craft 
Advisories for parts of Thursday, especially across southern 
sections of the Chesapeake Bay. A cold front tracks across the 
waters on Friday morning which favors a shift to north to 
northeasterly winds. These could near advisory criteria, but 
confidence is low. High pressure passing by to the north will 
result in a shift to east-southeasterlies for Saturday. Gusts up
to 15 to perhaps 20 knots are possible.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Current tidal anomalies remain around zero feet. However, expect
a gradual rise in water levels later today as high pressure 
pulls away from the Eastern Seaboard. This again pushes a number
of sites into Action stage during the higher of the two 
astronomical high tides, particularly tonight and again late
Wednesday.
